gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans: Unbroken monoline strokes, as if drawn with a round-tipped pen, give Oxanium its commanding look up top. But make it small and that character fades, whereas Noto Sans, with its generous c, holds steady at any size.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Crisp lines up top, generous curves below. Oxanium traces its glyphs in a single stroke width while Noto Sans Adlam keeps its curve endings well apart, so headline and text feel related yet clearly different.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoin: Commanding from the first glance, Oxanium looks like thin steel rod bent into every letter. Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined offers generous space between curve ends and stems, so it can be sized down without crowding.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hi: Oxanium sets a display heading with zero modulation in its line, a high x-height making lowercase look big. Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs, a sans-serif, has outward-pointing terminals and an x-height near cap height, which keeps text moving smoothly.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic gives its small letters generous openings. Oxanium brings commanding headings whose o forms a ring with a constant wall, and that firm shape gives the open text below something to lean on.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Oxanium draws true monoline letters with a high x-height that makes lowercase look big. And it earns its keep when big and short, leaving Noto Sans Armenian and its wide, inviting openings to do the quieter work.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Oxanium holds a stroke free of swell and thinning. What binds them most is openness: Noto Sans Avestan keeps curve tips apart, and Oxanium's curves end in clear daylight too.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Distinctive from the first line, Oxanium holds its strokes with the steadiness of a drawn string, tall in the lowercase. Noto Sans Balinese then gives it breathing room inside every curve.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Commanding, with strokes like cut ribbon of constant width. Oxanium leads that way, while Noto Sans Bamum, with big open counters in every small letter, gives the text below room to breathe.
gen-gf-oxanium-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Noto Sans Bassa Vah reads big in the middle, its dominant midsection swallowing the line's height. But Oxanium, drawn like stout pipe cleaner, is the one to command attention, while the sans-serif text quietly does the reading.
